The current issue report describes that the `PosixParser` class ignores unrecognized tokens starting with '-' when the `stopAtNonOption` parameter is enabled. This results in the token being simply ignored instead of being handled properly.

Looking at the `parse` method of the `PosixParser` class, we see that it has the following signature and description:
```java
public CommandLine parse(Options options, String[] arguments, boolean stopAtNonOption) throws ParseException
```
This method parses the specified arguments based on the specified `Options`. The `stopAtNonOption` parameter specifies whether to stop interpreting the arguments when a non-option has been encountered and to add them to the `CommandLine` args list.

From the failing test snippet, it's evident that the test is trying to parse arguments that include an unrecognized option (`-z`). The test then expects an `UnrecognizedOptionException` to be thrown, which is not currently happening due to the behavior described in the bug report.

To diagnose the bug, we need to investigate how the `PosixParser` class handles unrecognized options when `stopAtNonOption` is enabled and why the `UnrecognizedOptionException` is not being thrown as expected in this case.

Next, I will examine the relevant code to identify the root cause of the issue.
